defects: The turned profiles and dished seat are present, but reversed custom surface winding appears to leave large faces poorly lit or visible from their backs; v004 is substantially darker than v003 in the same room capture.
The seat perimeter transitions directly into a hard side wall, so the target’s softened sculpted edge and shallow dish are weakly expressed.
The lathed legs and posts have uncapped ends, and the small dark pegs do not make fitted joints legible at normal inspection distance.
hard_fail_reasons: The run-002 production views have dark, visually muddy surfaces and unresolved manufacturing transitions; the strict realism and craftsmanship gates fail.
incumbent_comparison: Compared with v003, v004 replaces the slab seat, straight cylindrical stretchers and plain back members with a dished seat surface, turned profiles, swept crest and shaped spindles. The silhouette now reads clearly as a chair and the envelope stays within the 25 x 19 x 23 inch brief, although the lower bounds extend 0.07 inch below the floor. In the run-002 production renders, the wood is much too dark, seat shaping and edge transitions are hard to read, and several turned members have visibly open ends. This is a meaningful geometry advance but not production-ready.
next_action_hypothesis: Keep the round-02 target and the authored-mesh approach. Correct custom triangle winding to match Godot front-face convention, cap the exposed leg ends, introduce a narrow rolled seat perimeter, and raise the wood tone for this authored-mesh refinement. Regenerate and inspect the production views before deciding whether this geometry approach can be reused.

observations.art_direction_fit: The new silhouette follows the generated round-02 target more closely than v003, but the target’s warm, shaped joinery and softly finished seat are not yet carried into the render.
observations.close_up_quality: The detail and interior-oblique views reveal uncapped turned members, hard seat edges and small low-contrast pegs.
observations.gameplay_readability: The gameplay-distance view reads as a chair, though the dark frame loses separation between seat, crest and supports.
observations.geometric_detail: Custom turned legs, shaped spindles, swept crest, tenon pins and a dished seat replace primitive straight members, although end caps and soft transitions are absent.
observations.material_realism: The same room capture makes v004 timber markedly darker than v003; the grain is barely legible on the seat and the wood planes blend into one dark mass.
observations.proportion: Measured extents are 23.58 x 18.84 x 20.75 inches against a 25 x 19 x 23 inch limit; the chair reads low and broad as intended, with a 0.07 inch floor penetration.
observations.scale_fidelity: The mesh bounds remain within the authoritative width, height and depth limits; only the lowest vertex is 0.07 inch below y=0.
observations.semantic_recognizability: The four legs, seat, three spindles and crest make the object unambiguously chair-shaped in the production room and isolated views.
observations.silhouette_quality: The curved crest and separated spindles improve the silhouette over v003, but the rear posts and crest remain dark and less readable than the target.
observations.surface_variation: Directional grain remains present but is muted by the dark tone and is not varied by board or member.
observations.technical_integration: Godot 4.7.2 generated and rendered the candidate through the production capture path, with 29 meshes, 29 surfaces, 40,736 triangles and no technical validation issues.

close_inspection.evidence: The detail and oblique captures show an unsoftened seat perimeter, exposed ends on turned members, and pegs that barely separate from the timber.

edge_treatment.evidence: The dish is shallow and its perimeter turns into a hard, angular side wall rather than the target’s softly shaped seat edge.

hardware.evidence: The target calls for a wooden chair without metal hardware; the authored wooden tenon pegs are appropriate in material, though their scale and contrast need improvement.

joins.evidence: Tenon pins are modeled but too small and dark to communicate fitted leg, stretcher and seat joints.

manufacturing_detail.evidence: Custom turning and crest geometry are advances, but open ends, hard seat edges and weakly legible joins remain visible.

material_response.evidence: The wood render is markedly darker than v003 and suppresses the grain and part-to-part separation.

surface_variation.evidence: Directional wood grain is barely visible on the dark seat and is repeated without board-level variation.

thickness.evidence: The seat slab, stretcher members and turned posts have continuous, plausible visible thickness in the room and detail views.

neutral_viewer_realism.evidence: The v004 production view reads as a chair, but its seat and frame collapse into a dark red-brown mass; custom surface orientation and hard transitions make it feel unfinished beside the approved target.

photo_character.evidence: The ArtBrief uses an approved generated target and has no source photograph.

visual_transfer_diagnosis.corrective_action: Retain the custom mesh strategy and round-02 target. Correct triangle winding to Godot front-face convention, close exposed lathe ends, form a narrow rolled seat edge, and raise timber tone for this mesh refinement. Render again before considering broader reuse.
lost_visual_information: The target’s warm wood value and clear separation between seat, crest, posts and turned members are lost in the dark production render.
The seat dish and softened perimeter do not read clearly because the surface meets a hard side wall.
The target’s fitted construction remains weak: turned ends are open and the wooden pins are too small and low-contrast.
preserved_components: The chair silhouette now includes a dished seat, turned legs and back posts, shaped spindles, a curved crest and separate stretchers.
The mesh remains within the 25 x 19 x 23 inch envelope apart from 0.07 inch floor penetration.
RoomDefinition placement and gameplay state are unchanged; the candidate is review-only.
